To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IFNβ rapidly induces the expression of cellular miRNAs and these miRNAs inhibit the replication of HCV.

(1) IFNβ rapidly induces the expression of cellular miRNAs; (2) IFNβ-induced cellular miRNAs target HCV RNA; (3) the antiviral activity of IFNβ can be reproduced by the ectopic expression of IFNβ-induced HCV-targeting miRNAs; and (4) IFNβ induces the expression of miR122, which has been shown to promote HCV replication, and this induction is important for IFNβ

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IFNα and IFβ induce miRNAs that are capable of targeting HCV RNAs, and that these miRNAs contribute to the antiviral activity of IFNs.
the authors have shown that miRNA expression is modulated by type I IFNs and that some miRNAs are involved in IFN-mediated antiviral activity against HCV.
the IFNβ-induced cellular miRNAs are important antiviral molecules in mammals, but that their effects may be more limited than those of the type I IFN system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miRNAs are important for antiviral defence in mammals, and that they are induced by IFNβ.
the innate immune system is a very powerful antiviral system, and that type I interferons are the major components of this antiviral system.
the IFNs are the primary mediators of the antiviral state in mammalian cells, and that the IFNs use multiple mechanisms to achieve their antiviral effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IFN response to viral infections in mammals can involve miRNAs, and that this may be important for antiviral defence.
the innate immune response to viral infection involves the induction of cellular miRNAs to suppress the replication of the virus.
IFNs are not the only way in which cells fight off viruses and that there is another layer of regulation that is mediated by miRNAs.
